about:
Blueprint Custom Apparel was established in 2019 in Derry, New Hampshire. The company operates from its New England base, providing custom-branded apparel and promotional products to a range of organizational clients.

The shop specializes in screen printing and embroidery, producing custom sweatshirts, jackets, hats, T-shirts, and a variety of branded accessories such as outerwear, workwear, and safety gear. Its services cover the full decoration process, from artwork preparation to final stitching or ink application, serving both small-run and bulk orders.

Blueprint works with small businesses, schools, U.S. government agencies, universities, enterprises, and startups, supplying apparel for trade shows, corporate events, and everyday uniform programs. The customer list reflects a focus on institutional and commercial buyers seeking consistent branding across multiple garment types.

The company emphasizes a direct, account-based approach: each client is assigned a dedicated sales representative to manage orders from quote through delivery. Blueprint also highlights its commitment to materials, craftsmanship, and repeatable quality, positioning its New England production as a mark of local excellence.

about:
Mahogany House Woodworks, operating as Boise Custom Furniture, is based in Boise, Idaho, and was founded in 2001 by James Barrett. Barrett came from a construction and high-end home building background before turning his lifelong passion for woodworking into a full-time shop. The business began with a focus on custom furniture built to last, using responsibly sourced materials and clean building methods.

The company designs and builds a range of custom wood products including dining tables, coffee tables, beds, headboards, bookshelves, floating shelves, adjustable desks, workstations, and commercial furniture for restaurants. They also produce custom wood countertops, butcher blocks, and cutting boards, and offer furniture engraving.

Mahogany House serves residential clients throughout Idaho and surrounding areas, as well as commercial customers such as restaurants and offices. Past projects include large bookcases for homes, bar tops for commercial spaces, and custom cutting boards for gifts.

Barrett positions the shop as an alternative to mass-produced furniture, emphasizing handcrafted construction, responsible material use, and a collaborative design process that provides clients with updates and photos during fabrication. The company offers free quotes and aims to deliver furniture that fits the client's budget and space.

name: Bond's Brewing Company-Buffalo
old_description: At Bond’s Brewing Company, our standard beers offer a little something for everyone, ensuring that every guest finds a brew they love. Crafted with high-quality ingredients, each beer highlights our dedication to excellence and balance. We strive to keep these favorites on tap year-round, providing a consistent selection of well-crafted brews that you can count on for any occasion.
about:
Founded in 2019 in Laramie, Wyoming, Bond's Brewing Company began as a passion project to craft unique, high-quality beer and foster a welcoming community space. From the start, the brewery focused on developing its own distinct recipes, aiming to reflect a dedication to craftsmanship and flavor in every pint.

The company produces a lineup of standard beers available year-round across its two Wyoming taprooms in Laramie and Buffalo, along with seasonal offerings. Its portfolio includes styles such as a red ale, fruited wheat ale, kolsch, Scottish ale, and hop-forward pale ale, all brewed with ingredients like specialty malts, Yakima Valley hops, and fresh fruit. In 2023, the Buffalo location expanded the concept by adding a craft cocktail program made with high-quality ingredients, including house-made mixes such as a clam-juice Michelada and a pickle-juice variant. The brewery operates as both a production facility and a hospitality venue, though specific facility size, headcount, and annual volume are not disclosed.

Bond's Brewing serves locals and visitors seeking a community-oriented craft beverage experience. Its beers and cocktails are sold directly through its taprooms, and the company collaborates with other small businesses for events and partnerships. The brand positions itself within Wyoming's growing craft beverage scene, targeting craft beer enthusiasts, tourists, and residents looking for a gathering place.

The company states that community is at the core of its mission, viewing beer as an experience that brings people together. It emphasizes innovation, quality, and a commitment to contributing to the vibrant culture of Wyoming. The addition of cocktails in Buffalo reflects a desire to offer guests more options while maintaining the same creative standards applied to its beer.

old_description: Industrial applications are evolving - and so are we. BorgWarner applies deep engineering expertise and advanced manufacturing capabilities to deliver solutions tailored to today’s industrial performance requirements.
about:
BorgWarner Inc. is headquartered in Hanover Park, Illinois. The company designs and manufactures systems for industrial and automotive applications, applying deep engineering expertise and advanced manufacturing capabilities to deliver solutions tailored to evolving industrial performance requirements.

Its product portfolio centers on battery energy storage systems (BESS), including generator battery systems, uninterruptible power supply units, and turbine generator systems. The company operates a production and service footprint across North America and Europe, with over 5 GWh of production capacity supported by a global supply base for cells and components. Core processes encompass full mechanical, electrical, testing, and validation capabilities, engineering services, and remanufacturing to extend product life. A removable electronics unit (RCB) enables easy service and repair.

BorgWarner serves industrial energy storage markets, providing stationary energy storage based on high-energy NMC battery technology for grid interaction and energy optimization. Customers deploy modular platforms ranging from rack-level backup to multi-megawatt-hour installations, addressing needs from seconds to hours of discharge duration.

The company differentiates itself through a cell-agnostic hardware and software architecture, automotive-grade battery management with redundant safety architecture, and a common hardware foundation that enables rapid deployment across power and energy scales.

about:
Boston Electronics operates from Brookline, Massachusetts. For forty years it has served as a distributor of electro-optical solutions, though a specific founding year is not disclosed.

The firm distributes advanced electro-optical components and specialized systems for microscopy, offering a broad portfolio that includes UV sensors and probes (SiC photodiodes), UV LEDs (255–405 nm), infrared detectors and imaging arrays (InGaAs PIN/APD, InAsSb, T2SLS), terahertz sources and imagers (QCL-based), photon-counting modules (TCSPC/FLIM), quantum cascade lasers, and laboratory instrumentation such as blackbody sources and laser power meters. It provides knowledgeable application support to help customers select and integrate these technologies.

Customers span environmental monitoring, process control, scientific instrumentation, life sciences and biomedical technologies, building and home automation, security and surveillance, and microscopy. The company works with researchers and manufacturers developing products for water and air purification, curing, lidar, thermal imaging, and spectroscopy.

Boston Electronics positions itself as a specialist in photo-detection and photon generation, representing manufacturers worldwide—including Hamamatsu, Becker & Hickl, Alpes Lasers, and Gentec-EO—to bring advantaged, unique-performance solutions to a broad market. Its stated differentiator is close collaboration with customers to address sensor requirements across diverse applications.

name: Boulder Furniture Arts
old_description: HEY, WE'RE BFA — CHAMPIONS OF SIMPLICITY, BASED IN BOULDER SINCE 1985. OUR FURNITURE IS BUILT FROM UNMATCHED AMERICAN HARDWOOD AND DESIGNED FOR LIFELONG JOY.
about:
Boulder Furniture Arts, a fine furniture design and build studio, has operated from Boulder, Colorado since its founding in 1985.

The firm produces two distinct lines: BFA Classic, a collection of largely unchanged designs dating back to 1985, and BFA Create, a custom arm that develops one-of-a-kind pieces including live-edge tables, built-in cabinetry, and mixed-material installations such as walnut-and-steel podiums or resin river tables. Production follows a 1-person-1-piece fabrication model supported by a 10-year apprenticeship program, with finishing limited to hand-rubbed oils and custom-matched commercial options. The shop also handles delivery, full-service installation, shipping, and a lifetime care program covering repair, refinishing, disassembly, and relocation.

Clients range from architects and interior designers who require precise collaboration to residents and families seeking heirloom-quality furnishings. The company also serves institutional leaders, artists, and environmentally conscious buyers who value carbon-storing materials.

Boulder Furniture Arts distinguishes itself by sourcing all hardwoods within a two-day drive of its shop, guaranteeing every piece for life, and rejecting surplus inventory. The founders frame the business as an “old-school working art house run by people who give a damn,” emphasizing analog modern aesthetics, playful restraint, and a direct maker-to-client relationship.

name: Boxcar Woody (Reclaimed Lumber)
old_description: During those pioneering years, one car stood out among the rest, almost as important as the locomotive engine itself: the boxcar. Not just because of the versatility for the freight it could carry, but because of the connection with humanity it offered. The typical boxcar doubled as a passenger car for the ticketless. It was even sometimes left behind in those newly founded towns as a shelter or, for others, a home. It provided an escape for those wanting to run from his or her current predicament or a ride to a better life. Often, the boxcar’s walls were a sounding board for a newly penned song or where a life drew its very first and, sometimes, sadly, last breath. The American Boxcar was all of this and more to both early Americans and Immigrants alike.
about:
Boxcar Woody operates from Stockyards City in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma. The business traces its roots to 2015, when the founders of Boxcar Revival embarked on a road trip to salvage materials from retired American boxcars. That experience inspired the creation of Boxcar Woody, a venture dedicated to reclaiming authentic freight lumber and giving it new life in homes and businesses nationwide.

The company selects, mills, and finishes reclaimed boxcar and cargo wood, as well as whiskey barrel staves, in its Oklahoma workshop. From these materials it produces raw lumber, countertops, mantels, and a range of finished goods including dining tables, chairs, barstools, lighting, barn doors, and accessories. Each piece is handcrafted and can be made to order in custom sizes, with no two items exactly alike.

Its reclaimed wood has been used for kitchen countertops, island tops, bathroom vanities, sliding barn doors, bar tops with waterfall edges, and exterior tables. The company also offers a line of whiskey barrel products such as chairs, barrels, and serving trays.

The founders started Boxcar Woody to preserve the legacy of the American railroads by turning historic materials into functional, lasting pieces. They emphasize quality craftsmanship and the unique character that comes from decades of service on the rails, positioning the reclaimed lumber as a connection to the nation’s transportation history.

about:
Boyko Inc. was founded in August 1987 in Stanton, North Dakota, by brothers Ron and Tom Boyko as a USDA‑inspected food manufacturing plant. The family‑owned corporation initially produced bakery and meat products before expanding into additional food items.

After two decades of manufacturing, the company sold its production operations in 2006 to focus on the used equipment market. Since 1996 Boyko has bought and sold used food‑processing machinery, and by 2002 it was doing so full‑time, sourcing equipment at auctions nationwide and partnering with auction firm Schneider Industries. Today the firm operates as a distributor and service provider, offering equipment listings, consignment sales, liquidations, asset‑management programs, technical support, and process‑plant consulting for food‑processing facilities.

The company serves food‑manufacturing customers across the processing industry, helping them acquire or dispose of equipment such as mixers, ovens, conveyors, packaging lines, and freezing systems. Its client base includes plants seeking individual machines or complete production lines, though no specific customers are named in public materials.

Boyko emphasizes its manufacturing heritage as a differentiator, stating that its background gives the team a diverse understanding of the requirements, challenges, and goals of food‑processing companies. The family‑owned business cites a mission to provide efficient, reliable service with the utmost integrity.

old_description: Vertically integrated LED chip maker (epitaxial wafers to light engines)
about:
Bridgelux operates from Fremont, California, where it develops and manufactures LED semiconductor products. The company is led by CEO Yiqun Li, though its founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed in the available materials.

The company describes itself as a vertically integrated LED chip maker, controlling production from epitaxial wafers through finished light engines. Its product portfolio includes the RGBW Series flagship platform, F90™ technology that aims to deliver high color rendering without sacrificing efficacy, Thrive™ LEDs designed to mimic natural light spectra, and flexible LED strip solutions for architectural and commercial applications. Recent expansions have added high-power outdoor lighting platforms and flexible linear light offerings.

Bridgelux serves the LED lighting industry broadly, with specific focus on architectural, commercial, and outdoor lighting markets. Its components are designed for integration into luminaires and lighting systems where color quality, tunability, and efficacy are specified. The company has announced strategic partnerships, including a patent cross-licensing agreement with Lumitech for next-generation tunable white and RGBW color-mixing technology.

Bridgelux positions its vertical integration as a core differentiator, allowing control over the entire LED production chain from wafer to light engine. These innovations are framed as giving customers a competitive advantage in lighting performance.

Bridgeport Insulated Wire Co. was established in 1950 in Bridgeport, Connecticut. The company has operated continuously from its original location, producing insulated wire products entirely within the United States.

The company manufactures a range of insulated wire including magnet wire, Litz wire, textile-served wire, and custom bobbin-wound constructions. Its Bridgeport facility houses in-house designed equipment for wire drawing, enameling, twisting, stranding, tinning, bobbin winding, and textile serving, supporting over 12 enamel insulation types from Class 105 to Class 220.

Bridgeport Insulated Wire serves manufacturers in the electrical, aircraft, instrumentation, television, motor, and defense industries. Its products are specified for transformers, solenoids, fractional motors, synchros, relays, aircraft systems, instruments, controls, and military equipment.

The company emphasizes its military and government approvals—including NEMA MW-1000 and Naval JW-1177/A—and its engineering department consults on insulation selection and specification compliance. All manufacturing occurs at the Connecticut plant, which the company says keeps quality high, lead times short, and communication direct.

Burmeister Woodwork Co operates from Hales Corners, Wisconsin, just south of Milwaukee. The business traces its origins to the early 1920s when Marvin Burmeister founded Advance Millwork; the name was changed to Burmeister Woodwork in 1937. It remained in the Burmeister family for three generations—George Burmeister took over in 1964 and added stair fabrication, and his son Russell Burmeister shifted the focus to high‑end custom architectural millwork in 1981. In 2015, John Sprenger, a military veteran, acquired the company and serves as president.

Its 40,000‑square‑foot manufacturing facility in Hales Corners houses a team of about 60 craftsmen who engineer, fabricate, finish, and install each piece. A branch office in Chicago supports project coordination across the Midwest and nationally. The shop combines traditional hand craftsmanship with modern technology and regularly incorporates custom veneers, exotic wood species, metal, glass, and upholstery into complex, technically demanding projects.

Burmeister serves the luxury residential market—creating millwork for high‑end homes, penthouses, and historic renovations—and the commercial sector, with projects such as a modern bank lobby. Clients include architects, designers, and builders throughout the Midwest and across the United States who bring the company their most challenging custom woodwork requirements.

John Sprenger has said he was drawn to the company because of its culture of craftsmanship and the pursuit of excellence he learned in the military, a philosophy that continues to drive the firm’s focus on uncompromising artisanship and turning bold design ideas into reality.

Its quality system targets a first-pass yield above 99%, warranty returns below 0.5%, and on-time delivery exceeding 97%, supported by ISO 9001:2015 and ISO 13485:2016 certifications, Lean manufacturing, and Six Sigma methodologies.

about:
C & C Manufacturing Inc. operates from Gaithersburg, Maryland, where the business traces its roots to 1974. Boyhood friends Ron Crupi and Scott Campbell formed a partnership to build custom trailers and towing components, launching the Mastertrack brand. In 2012, Dawn Crupi, daughter of one founder, established C & C Manufacturing Inc. to carry forward her father’s legacy, keeping the company family-owned.

The company manufactures the Mastertrack line of trailers — including dump, enclosed, landscape, and equipment models — and maintains a rotating inventory of new and used units. Its shop provides full-service trailer repair, custom fabrication, steel and aluminum welding, electrical work, and Maryland-authorized state and DOT inspections. An in-stock parts department supplies axles, brakes, suspensions, tires, wheels, lighting, cargo hardware, and Dexter Axle components, while the team also installs hitches, gooseneck and fifth-wheel systems, tow-vehicle wiring, and brake controllers.

Customers range from federal agencies such as NASA, the U.S. Navy, the U.S. Army, and the White House to commercial haulers, landscapers, construction firms, and individual trailer owners. The business serves both government contracts and the retail market, offering sales, service, and inspection for a wide variety of towing needs.

From the start, the founders emphasized quality over volume, choosing to build trailers one at a time rather than pursue large-scale expansion. That philosophy remains central: the company states that superior trailers result from focused, piece-by-piece fabrication and a commitment to fast turnaround on repairs.

The company emphasizes continuous improvement, reinvesting profits into new technology and cloud‑based workflow tools to shorten lead times and improve quality. Its single‑source model covers cutting, bending, fabricating, and welding, aiming to deliver high‑quality metal parts on schedule.

The founders started the business to meet a hospitality-industry need for decorated uniforms, and the company says its differentiating factor is the rare complete in-house facility that controls every step from art to finished goods. The business has remained locally owned and operated throughout its history, expanding in 2001 by joining forces with Rocky Mountain Cabinets, a fellow Colorado Springs cabinet maker that shared its focus on craftsmanship and customer satisfaction.

Today the company functions as both a major hardwood retailer and a custom woodworking facility, describing itself as one of the largest such operations in El Paso County. Its shop produces custom cabinetry, architectural millwork, live‑edge slab furniture, and other made‑to‑order wood products, while its showroom and lumber yard stock domestic and exotic hardwoods, softwoods, plywood, mouldings, and a wide selection of finished and unfinished furniture, including Amish‑crafted pieces. The facility also offers a complimentary cut‑to‑size service on sheet goods.

The customer base spans homeowners, contractors, woodworkers, builders, remodelers, interior designers, and craftsmen. Builders and remodelers source cabinetry and millwork for residential projects; woodworkers and hobbyists purchase lumber, plywood, and live‑edge slabs for custom projects; and homeowners buy finished furniture or commission bespoke pieces. The company notes that its custom woodworking shop serves enthusiasts, homeowners needing specific furniture, and businesses seeking unique pieces for their spaces.

The founding mission — to build quality products and ensure every customer receives exactly what they envisioned — remains the stated differentiator. Leadership emphasizes that owner‑operated status allows personalized attention, expert guidance, and a commitment to craftsmanship that has earned the trust of the local building and woodworking community over four decades.

The team reports more than 1,000 completed projects and over 500 clients across 25-plus years.

Clients span small startups to large enterprises throughout the Denver metro region, including Centennial, Littleton, Westminster, Boulder, and Parker. The company also supports individual customers and has assisted telecom technicians in other states with troubleshooting. Long-term relationships are common; one client cited over 20 years of continuous service for telephone equipment and repair.

CTAC Solutions emphasizes a customer-centric model that promises direct human support without automated phone trees. The 2024 rebrand marked a shift from a traditional telecom provider to a full-spectrum solutions partner, aiming to deliver scalable, future-ready technology with minimal disruption during installation and maintenance.

Founded to meet urgent wartime needs, Cadillac Products emphasizes full vertical integration under one roof, 100% U.S.-based production, and rapid prototyping that can verify concepts in days. Cajun Original Foods, Inc. was founded in 1988 in New Iberia, Louisiana, the heart of Cajun Country. The company operates a USDA- and FDA-inspected plant where it produces a line of traditional Cajun foods.

The product lineup includes boudin balls, boudin sausage, boudin party links, pistolettes, Cajun pies, and a range of sauces. The company also offers private-label manufacturing for other brands. All items are made using family recipes passed down through generations, with meat products carrying USDA certification and sauces and seafood items under FDA oversight. The facility has been in operation for over 38 years.

Cajun Original Foods emphasizes its heritage recipes and the balance of flavor—“not bland, but not too hot”—as its defining difference.

name: Cal Manufacturing
old_description: Resistance Welding Technologies, Cables, Shunts & Accessories - Division of CAL Manufacturing, Inc
about:
Cal Manufacturing, Inc. operates from Vicksburg, Michigan. The woman-owned company has over 50 years of experience in resistance welding technologies, though a specific founding year is not publicly stated. Cheryl Benson serves on the board of trustees overseeing daily operations, sales, and marketing, while Russ Hayward manages the plant with a background in welding and millwright work.

The company manufactures a range of resistance welding products including air-cooled and water-cooled jumpers, dual-conductor "Kickless" cables, the patented Swivel King kickless cable, induction furnace cables, and copper laminated shunts. It also produces cable adapters, busbars, and water-cooled cable adapters using CNC machining for higher tolerances. Additional services include cable repair and rebuilding, recycling, and custom cable design for robotic welding applications.

Cal Manufacturing serves the automotive industry, supplying OEMs, distributors, and Tier I, II, and III companies, with a growing presence in Mexico for export. Its products are also used in the broader resistance welding and robotics welding markets, where the company emphasizes industrial cable management to reduce failure rates.

The company differentiates itself through expedited shipping programs offering same-day or next-day delivery on stocked items, a patented Swivel King cable that allows 180-degree rotation with minimal force, and a commitment to inspecting and testing every product before shipment. Founded on the principle of being a complete cable supplier, Cal Manufacturing aims to turn customer emergencies into its own priority.

name: Calgreg Electronics Inc
about:
Calgreg Electronics operates from Warwick, Rhode Island, where founder Robert Mazzeo established the business to address a gap he saw in the electronics supply chain. Mazzeo recognized that manufacturers needed more than just component delivery—they required rapid engineering support, inventory management, and a suite of value-added services from a single distribution partner.

The company distributes a broad line of electronic and electromechanical components—interconnects, thermal management products, wedge-loks, rugged card guides, enclosures, and enclosure hardware—while also providing in-house design, testing, and assembly services.

The firm’s vendor-managed inventory and design capabilities are aimed at customers looking to reduce procurement overhead and accelerate product development cycles.

The company’s differentiation rests on combining distribution with technical services that are typically sourced separately. By integrating design, test, and thermal analysis under one roof, Calgreg aims to give customers “tactically quick” engineering support while managing inventory risk through its Asian supply network. and global divisions.

Cali-Fabworks was founded in 2001 in Anaheim, California, and operates from a facility on East Miraloma Avenue. The company is led by CEO Bryan Rios and focuses on architectural metal fabrication for both residential and commercial clients.

The shop produces custom gates, steel and glass doors, railings, bar cabinets, shelving, fireplace doors, and other bespoke metalwork. Its in-house process covers design, fabrication, powder coating with baked zinc primer, metallization, and installation. The company serves Orange County and surrounding cities including Newport, Laguna, Orange, Tustin, and Irvine.

Customers range from homeowners seeking custom entry gates and interior railings to businesses needing storefront doors, office partitions, and commercial stair railings. Recent projects include exterior entry doors, sliding and French doors, pivot doors, and aluminum gates for rust protection.

Cali-Fabworks emphasizes a quality control system backed by a 100% satisfaction guarantee, precision craftsmanship by certified professionals, on-time delivery, and the use of premium materials for weather-resistant results. The company highlights direct local service without middlemen as a core differentiator.

about:
Calico Design Manufacturing, LLC was founded in 2017 in East Los Angeles, California. The studio operates from Los Angeles, serving the local community and a broader client base.

The company specializes in themed environments, decorative arts, and specialty millwork. Its capabilities span scenic arts — including gold leaf gilding, hand-lettered signage, scenic finishes, and patinas — and specialty fabrication such as panel-goods processing, multi-axis CNC routing and carving, solid-wood machining, and full finishing. The studio also produces bespoke, one-of-a-kind objects for brands and showrooms. All work is managed in-house from design and engineering through final delivery.

Calico serves clients in hospitality, entertainment, and retail, with project experience for restaurants, hotels, theaters, attractions, studios, and brands. The firm applies craft traditions from film and television set construction to permanent installations.

The company distinguishes itself by combining scenic artistry and precision millwork under a single team, project management process, and design sensibility, eliminating the need for clients to coordinate separate vendors. It also commits to responding to project inquiries with a realistic timeline within 48 hours.

name: California Plastix
old_description: All products from California Plastix are inspected for quality and consistency by trained employees.  Nothing leaves our factory without inspection.
about:
California Plastix operates from Pomona, California, where it produces custom poly bags and polyethylene film for a national customer base. The company was founded on the principle of delivering reliable, American-made packaging with the flexibility to meet any specification, though a specific founding year is not publicly disclosed.

The manufacturer runs fully integrated extrusion, flexographic printing, and converting operations under one roof. Printing presses handle up to six colors with a registration tolerance of ±1/32 inch. The converting department fabricates side-weld, bottom-seal, gusseted, wicketed, zipper, and tape bags in widths of 3 to 60 inches and lengths up to 72 inches, including wicket counts of 250 to 1,000 bags per wicket. The facility also supplies tubing, sheeting, centerfold film, and roll stock.

California Plastix serves food and beverage processors, bakeries, industrial manufacturers, retail and e-commerce packagers, medical and pharmaceutical suppliers, agricultural operations, and wholesale distributors. Its products flow through supply chains that support major retailers such as Costco, The Home Depot, Trader Joe’s, Target, and Bloomingdale’s, though the company is not affiliated with those brands.

The company emphasizes its Southern California location, in-house production, and direct communication with the production team as key differentiators. It cites decades of hands-on industry experience, competitive pricing from vertical integration, and a commitment to consistent gauge control, strong seals, and fast, predictable lead times as reasons customers choose it.

old_description: As an experienced transportation equipment manufacturing facility, we offer vast fabrication and welding capabilities. These include rolling, bending, punching, heavy and specialized fabrication, heavy welding, CWI services, and custom sanitary welding. We can use carbon steel, stainless steel, Inconel, Monel, Hastelloy, or nickel in our custom fabrications.
about:
Cameron Manufacturing & Design operates from two facilities: a 145,000-square-foot plant in Horseheads, New York, and a 28,000-square-foot operation in Orlando, Florida. The company was founded in 1983 by Frank LaViola Sr. to address a regional need for custom fabrication in upstate New York. In 2007, LaViola transitioned the business to an Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP), making the workforce the company's owners.

The firm provides custom metal manufacturing across the full project lifecycle — engineering design, CNC machining (milling, lathing, waterjet and laser cutting), sheet metal fabrication (rolling, bending, punching), heavy and sanitary welding with CWI oversight, in-house finishing (powder coating, painting, vibratory tumbling), and on-site installation with documentation packages. The combined facilities employ hundreds of skilled workers.

Cameron serves food and dairy processors requiring USDA- and 3A-compliant equipment, rail and transit agencies needing custom metal components and signaling systems, and a mix of Fortune 500 and regional manufacturers seeking turnkey process equipment.

LaViola started the business as a local "fab shop" focused on quality workmanship, on-time delivery, and customer service. The ESOP structure was adopted to preserve that culture by vesting ownership in the employees who execute the work, a model the company credits for its ability to adapt across decades of industry change.

old_description: © 2026 Campo Sheet Metal Works Inc. | Custom Industrial Metal Work Since 1926
about:
Campo Sheet Metal Works, Inc. was founded in 1926 by Salvatore Campo in a Houston garage where he fabricated gutters and flashing. Nearly a century later, the company operates from a facility Building 15, in Houston, Texas, and remains family owned and operated with fourth‑generation family members active in the business.

The shop provides custom metal fabrication services including water jet cutting, press brake forming, plate rolling, structural rolling, shearing, plasma and oxyfuel cutting, metal punching and drilling, sawing, and welding. Equipment includes three CNC water jets, multiple press brakes, turret punches, plate rolls, structural rolls, saws, drill presses, and a robotic welding cell for repeatable welds on production parts. The company describes its operation as a one‑stop shop capable of handling complete turnkey projects or individual piece work.

Customers span oil and gas, aerospace, petrochemical, architectural, food and beverage plants, material handling, and marine industries. Examples cited include cutting 12‑1/2‑inch rod for a marine clevis and a range of custom steel fabrications for industrial and manufacturing markets.

The company emphasizes its family values of honesty, integrity, and respect in daily client interactions, and points to over nine decades of satisfied clients as evidence of its track record for delivering quality fabricated products on schedule.

about:
Carolina Textiles traces its origins to 1920, when Grossman Industries was founded in Columbus, Ohio. Now a fourth-generation family-owned business, the company is headquartered in Walterboro, South Carolina, where it opened its first dedicated facility in 1995. The firm expanded through acquisitions, adding a Greer, South Carolina location in 2013 via the purchase of American Wiping Cloth and an Atlanta, Georgia operation in 2016 with the acquisition of Mountain Textiles.

The company manufactures and distributes a range of wiping products, including colored, gray, and white knit rags, fleece, terry cloth, disposable paper wipes, and microfiber cloths. It processes recycled textiles, diverting more than 12 million pounds of material from landfills each year. Packaging options include hand-packed and machine-compressed boxes and bags in 5-, 10-, 25-, and 50-pound sizes. The management team brings over 40 years of experience in the wiping cloth and used clothing sectors.

Carolina Textiles serves distributors and end users across the southeastern United States, including South Carolina, North Carolina, Florida, Georgia, Kentucky, Tennessee, Mississippi, Alabama, and Virginia. Its products are used in automotive, marine, industrial, janitorial, and food-service applications. The company also operates a thrift-store partnership program that purchases unusable donated clothing for recycling.

The business emphasizes its long-standing commitment to recycling, stating that it has repurposed used textiles since its inception. It also highlights customer service, an extensive product line, convenient ordering, affordable pricing, and fast delivery as key differentiators.

name: Carson Manufacturing Inc
old_description: After 48 years of operations, the company is well-known, a leading manufacturer of planetary gearheads. And, of course, the innovation didn’t stop in 1996.
about:
Carson Manufacturing Inc. is a family-owned manufacturer of planetary gearheads based in Carson City, Nevada. The company traces its roots to 1986, when Eddie Capps and his wife Barbara purchased the business. Three generations of the family have since guided the operation, including their daughter Delores Stacy, now vice president, and her son Kenny Penn, a sales engineer. A pivotal redesign in 1996 introduced a bearing-holder architecture that aligns gears along the centerline, a method that later became an industry standard.

The company produces several gearhead lines — Precision, Eliminator, “S” Series, and Right Angle (RE and RP) — covering sizes 17 through 56 and standard ratios from 3:1 to 100:1, with custom ratios up to 10,000:1. It maintains over 231 standard models and operates an internal research and development division where every design undergoes strenuous testing under multiple conditions. Custom gearheads are engineered to mount virtually any motor, and the company does not charge a design fee for custom work.

Customers span medical device makers (including cancer-detection equipment), paper-production machinery, motion-control and robotics integrators, aerospace programs such as Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University, HVAC manufacturers, and supply-chain automation firms like Attabotics. The company also serves servo-system distributors and industrial OEMs.

Carson Manufacturing emphasizes on-time, on-budget delivery, with standard units shipping in two days and custom designs completed in a week. All products are made entirely in the United States, avoiding tariffs and reducing shipping costs. The firm’s differentiators include the no-fee custom design policy, the 1996 bearing-holder innovation, and a testing regimen that validates each configuration before shipment.

about:
Casco Bay Molding was founded in February 2000 by Andrew Powell in Sanford, Maine, with a vision for producing silicone and thermoplastic products domestically. The company’s earliest offerings included a scuba line of mouthpieces, regulator straps, and octopus necklaces.

Today the firm operates as a vertically integrated, FDA‑registered, ISO 13485:2016‑certified product development and injection molding facility. Its Sanford factory houses an in‑house machine shop that builds and maintains precision tooling, enabling silicone and thermoplastic injection molding, over‑molding, ultrasonic welding, assembly, and inspection. The company reports over two decades of production experience and has manufactured more than one million menstrual cups for global B2B customers, alongside high‑volume runs of medical device components such as CPAP parts, surgical handles, valves, and custom gaskets.

Casco Bay Molding serves primarily the medical device sector (Class I and II), supplying OEMs, startups, and NGOs with products ranging from respiratory equipment and surgical instruments to menstrual health devices like the patented Flip Disc and Wandah applicator. The company also produces components for energy extraction, scuba gear, and PPE — notably the Casco Shield face shield developed during the COVID‑19 pandemic in partnership with Thermoformers of New England.

The business was started to keep silicone and thermoplastic manufacturing in the United States. Its differentiation lies in combining design, tooling, production, and regulatory support under one roof, reducing mold lead times and costs through in‑house toolmaking. The team’s background at firms such as Nypro, Netstal, and Shape, plus automation partnerships with EAM and Province Automation, supports a vertically integrated development cycle that the company says turns clinical insights into market‑ready devices.

Membership in the Work Truck Association (NTEA) connects the company with commercial vehicle manufacturers and distributors.

Gann started the business after seeing that his former employer had to outsource upfitting work miles away, and he believed other local businesses faced the same challenge. about:
Central Coast Live Foods operates from Watsonville, California, and traces its roots to 2014 when Central Coast Juicery opened its first location in Pacific Grove. The business was built around a mission to bring fresh, organic juice to the local community; a founder named Max is referenced in customer feedback discussing order fulfillment. What began as a juice shop evolved after customers repeatedly asked for more food options, the team to develop a single product that met their ingredient standards.

The company manufactures Kraut Krackers, a fermented cracker made from just four organic ingredients. The production process centers on fermentation, which the company says enhances nutrient absorption and provides probiotics, dietary fiber, electrolytes, and healthy fats. The crackers are soy-free, sugar-free, seed-oil-free, gluten-free, and vegan. From a kitchen that could not keep up with demand, production scaled to the point that the product now sits on retail shelves across California, serving hundreds of direct customers.

The primary buyers are health-focused consumers seeking gut-health support, including people with conditions such as Crohn's disease, as well as vegan and fitness-oriented shoppers looking for a post-workout snack with electrolytes. The product is positioned in the organic snack, functional food, and gut-health categories, sold both direct-to-consumer and through California retail accounts.

The founders say they created Kraut Krackers because it was the only food product that matched their criteria for nutrient-dense, minimally processed ingredients without ultra-processed additives. Customer demand outpaced their ability to make the crackers by hand, prompting them to ramp up production and expand distribution.

old_description: Central Sheet Metal Products is a family owned and operated precision sheet metal fabricator since 1912.
about:
Central Sheet Metal Products, Inc. has operated from Skokie, Illinois since its founding in 1912. The family-owned business, now in its fifth generation under the Silverstein family—Joel and Peter Silverstein representing the fourth generation and Ron and Rob Silverstein the fifth—began as a Chicago storefront supplying building materials such as copper, roof flashings, gutters, and downspouts. Over the decades it evolved through light stampings and wartime fabrication into a full-service OEM contract manufacturer.

The company specializes in precision sheet metal fabrication, producing brackets, enclosures, housings, chassis, faceplates, panels, covers, rack-mount components, and custom OEM part housings. Core processes include fiber laser cutting with lights-out automation, CNC bending and forming on multiple press brakes up to 135 metric tons, CNC turret punching, welding and spot welding, drilling, tapping, countersinking, hardware insertion, shearing, and vibratory finishing. In-house engineering uses SolidWorks 3D solid modeling for design, reverse engineering, and reengineering. The shop also manages contract finishing—powder coating, e-coating, painting, silk screening, plating, and anodizing—through long-standing vendor relationships. Capabilities span small, medium, and large volume runs with multiple part-mix flexibility.

Customers span OEM medical and dental devices, electronics, rack-mount and audio/visual equipment, computer peripherals, industrial machinery, electrical and air-handling systems, display and point-of-purchase fixtures, gaming, food and beverage vending, and agricultural equipment. The firm serves as a contract manufacturer for OEMs across these sectors.

The company cites its unchanged philosophy of quality craftsmanship and complete customer satisfaction as its differentiator, emphasizing direct communication, troubleshooting, on-time delivery, and repeat business. Continuous improvement drives capital investment in manufacturing technology, while incoming material inspection, calibrated measuring equipment, first-article inspection reports, and certificates of conformance underpin quality assurance. A long-standing delivery record with few disruptions supports its business-continuity motto: “what is good for you, is good for us.”

Chilton Furniture, based in Portland, Maine, traces its origins to 1885 when the Chilton Paint Co. began manufacturing paints, varnishes, and industrial coatings in Portland, Boston, and New York. Customer reviews highlight the company’s personal service and the ability to purchase without seeing pieces in person. The brand’s aesthetic centers on New England traditions and natural materials.

The company emphasizes that its furniture is handmade in the USA from premium natural materials, positioning itself as a steward of enduring craftsmanship.

name: Click Therapeutics
old_description: ™, and founded Click Therapeutics, which develops, validates, and commercializes software as prescription medical treatments for people with unmet medical needs.
about:
Click Therapeutics was founded in 2012 in New York City by David Benshoof Klein, who recognized the profound influence of smartphones on behavior and cognition. Klein coined the term "Digital Therapeutics™" and established the company to develop, validate, and commercialize software as prescription medical treatments for patients with unmet medical needs. The venture-backed firm counts HIG, Accelmed, and Sanofi Ventures among its investors.

The company operates a multimodal, AI-enabled platform that combines neuroscience with proprietary neuromodulatory mechanisms to create prescription digital therapeutics (PDTs) and Software-Enhanced Drugs™. Its pipeline includes CT-152 (Rejoyn™), an FDA-cleared adjunctive treatment for major depressive disorder developed with Otsuka; CT-155 (Motivista) for negative symptoms of schizophrenia; AspyreRx™ for type 2 diabetes; and CT-132 for episodic migraine, all of which have received FDA authorization. Additional candidates target opioid use disorder, multiple sclerosis, atopic dermatitis, obesity, oncology, insomnia, and acute coronary syndrome. A multidisciplinary team of clinicians, researchers, and technologists drives development from discovery through pivotal trials.

Click Therapeutics serves patients, prescribing physicians, and biopharma partners across the digital therapeutics, software-as-a-medical-device, and life-sciences sectors. Its treatments are regulated by the FDA and global authorities as medical devices and are prescribed and reimbursed as drug-software combination products.

The company's stated mission is to provide global access to safe and effective prescription digital therapeutics. Its differentiators include a platform-based approach that integrates clinically proven therapies with software-driven neuromodulation, a track record of first-of-kind FDA clearances, and a commitment to rigorous clinical validation through randomized controlled trials.

about:
ClickFold Plastics was founded in 2001 in Charlotte, North Carolina, to address a gap in the market for custom plastic enclosures and parts in smaller volumes. The company developed a zero-tooling fabrication process that eliminates the need for expensive molds, targeting industrial buyers who previously had to choose between off-the-shelf enclosures, costly injection molding, or sheet metal fabrication.

The company produces custom plastic housings, enclosures, covers, panels, and similar components using CNC machining, 3D printing, digital graphics, UV printing, EMI shielding, assembly, and packaging services. Its facility straddles the North Carolina–South Carolina border near Charlotte Douglas International Airport, operates multiple shifts in an air-conditioned, smoke-free environment, and focuses on just-in-time delivery for low-volume production runs.

ClickFold serves OEMs across industrial controls, medical devices, communications, gaming and simulators, building controls, measuring equipment, government and military, and commercial vehicles. Customers receive virtual 3D prototypes for review before physical first articles are produced using the same materials and processes as final production.

The zero-tooling approach allows cost-effective low-volume manufacturing with no minimum order quantities and a typical concept-to-production timeline of under four weeks. The quality system has been ISO 9001 certified since 2017, and the company maintains international production-transfer partnerships with firms in Germany and Brazil, as well as collaborations with local universities.

Colorado Microcircuits (CMI) operates a custom-built facility in Loveland, Colorado, specializing in highly automated contract assembly of microwave and RF semiconductors.

about:
Consolidated Telcom, headquartered in Dickinson, North Dakota, traces its roots to January 2, 1961, when the Bowman‑Slope Rural Telephone Mutual Aid Corporation and the Dunn Telephone Mutual Aid Corporation merged to form the Consolidated Telephone Cooperative. The cooperative is owned by its members—customers who use its services—and governed by an elected board of directors.

The company provides telecommunications services across southwestern North Dakota, including fiber‑to‑the‑home internet, cable television, voice, and business services such as cybersecurity and camera solutions. Since 2005 it has built a 100% fiber‑to‑the‑home network in its cooperative exchanges, serving 19 communities, and is extending fiber upgrades to its competitive local exchange carrier (CLEC) territory in Dickinson, Belfield, and Gladstone. Operations also include a CATV system acquired in 2000 that now covers the entire cooperative service area.

Consolidated serves residential and business customers in rural and small‑town markets across southwestern North Dakota. Its customer base includes households, farms, ranches, and enterprises such as Dickinson State University, which became its first CLEC client in 1998. The cooperative model aims to deliver urban‑level services at affordable rates to communities that larger carriers often overlook.

Founded to bring essential telephone service to areas where commercial providers found it unprofitable, the cooperative remains driven by its mission to “empower our communities by delivering advanced telecommunications products and services and building reliable, future‑ready infrastructure.” Its structure returns revenues above operating costs to members as capital credits, aligning incentives with customer needs rather than shareholder profit.

name: Corbitt Manufacturing Company
old_description: Since 1948 we have supported the transportation, construction, industrial tool, farm and foodservice industries. We deliver the top-quality products you need, when and where you need it. Guaranteed.
about:
Corbitt Manufacturing Company operates from a 100,000-square-foot facility in Paragould, Arkansas. Founded in 1948, the business began as a diversified contract manufacturer specializing in permanent-mold aluminum castings, machined components, custom tooling, and complete assemblies. In 2019, the company was acquired by The Greenbrier Companies and now operates as a Greenbrier subsidiary.

The plant houses three CNC machining centers and three furnaces feeding multiple pour lines, supported by grinders, broaching machines, milling machines, lathes, and a range of presses including a Dake 375-ton hydraulic press, a Bliss SC2 500-ton press, and a Niagara HBM 175-ton press. Standard permanent-mold castings run up to 75 pounds with a maximum mold envelope of 48 by 62 inches, while machining services cover prototype design, reverse engineering, wire and RAM EDM, gear cutting, jig and fixture building, and assembly. Production volumes span from one-off prototypes to several hundred thousand units annually.

Corbitt serves OEMs in earth-moving, mining, agricultural, electrical, transportation, recreation, and food-service markets. In transportation it produces dock cleats, transmission casings, manifolds, and railroad-car parts as the industry shifts from iron to aluminum. For food service it re-engineered a motor housing that eliminated leakage and cut scrap rates. Electrical work includes explosion-proof receptacles and power-line connectors, while powertrain projects focus on light- and heavy-duty gearboxes held to super-close tolerances.

The company emphasizes a "what you need, when and where you need it" delivery guarantee backed by in-house testing protocols that fast-track part deployment. Engineering staff provide troubleshooting expertise on every project, positioning Corbitt as a problem-solving partner rather than a pure production shop.

All parts are pre‑dismantled, cleaned, tested and shelved for immediate pickup or delivery.

Customers include body shops, insurance companies, fellow salvage yards and individual vehicle owners across northern Utah. The yard serves both commercial and retail buyers, offering a ready supply of recycled OEM parts for collision repair and maintenance.

Crabtree Auto distinguishes itself through membership in the Automotive Recyclers Association (ARA) and as a founding member of the United Recyclers Group (URG), adhering to URG quality standards for premium recycled parts. Its long‑standing slogan — “CLEAN – ORGANIZED – QUICK SERVICE” — reflects an emphasis on facility upkeep and fast turnaround.

name: Crossfire Technologies Inc
old_description: CrossFire’s Bridgelet products provide the Chiplet to Chiplet interconnect currently provided by Interposers, but without the cost, complexity or availability limitations.  Depending on system requirements, Bridgelets can be either passive or active.
about:
Crossfire Technologies Inc, headquartered in St. Paul, Minnesota, develops advanced chiplet interconnect solutions for the semiconductor industry. The company focuses on eliminating the need for traditional silicon interposers through its Bridgelet product line.

Crossfire’s core offerings include Bridgelets — passive or active interconnect devices that replace interposers for chiplet-to-chiplet communication — and Direct Chiplet Input/Output (DCIO), a streamlined PHY interface compatible with standard link layers such as UCIe and Bunch of Wires. The company also provides OmniDie, a proprietary integration capability that physically combines multiple chiplets into a single “SuperChip” mounted directly on a package substrate, reducing reliance on advanced packaging. These technologies support ultra-short-reach signaling (<500 µm), die-scale interconnect densities (sub-micron), and protocol-agnostic operation.

Its solutions are designed to enable chiplet reuse across product families and to disaggregate system I/O from memory functions.

Crossfire positions its technology as an interposer alternative that delivers up to 50× smaller form factor, 10× lower energy per bit, and 10× lower upfront cost, with up to 50 percent reduction in chiplet die area. The company states that its DCIO approach can achieve 10× lower power, cost, and higher density compared to competing solutions, while its OmniDie integration minimizes the need for costly advanced packaging.

old_description: We custom-build the highest quality cables right here in the USA.
about:
Custom Battery Cables LLC operates from Mesa, Arizona, where founder Vince launched the business in 2003 from a spare room in his home. The venture traces back to the late 1970s when Vince, then a student in a diesel and heavy equipment program at Maricopa Technical Community College, could not find quality battery cables for his 1948 Willy’s CJ-2A and began building his own. He later made cables for heavy construction equipment while working as a mechanic for firms such as Mountain Bell and Sunstate Equipment, then spent 29 years at Intel in electronics engineering roles before turning the side project into a full-time operation.

The company hand-builds made-to-order battery cables for cars, trucks, boats, RVs, golf carts, solar installations, and heavy equipment.

Customers span automotive, marine, solar, and heavy-equipment sectors, from classic-car restorers and high-output engine builders to snowplow operators and RV owners. The shop also serves bulk buyers through a dedicated bulk-order channel, supplying cables for fleet maintenance, construction equipment, and industrial applications.

Vince started the business because store-bought cables consistently fell short on durability; his original cables lasted 20 years without corrosion or overheating. The company emphasizes that it uses higher-grade wire than typical OEM or auto-parts-store offerings, avoids cost-cutting on materials, and builds each cable to withstand extreme temperatures and demanding starting conditions.

Its customer base ranges from regional operators to national brands, including foodservice operators, restaurant chains, retailers, and institutional customers. The Founder’s Pride™ line provides ready-to-order frozen dough products for distribution and foodservice operations nationwide.

The company emphasizes its founder-owned structure as a source of flexibility and personal service. It holds SQF Level A certification, an AIB Superior rating, and Kosher certification, and operates a HACCP-based food safety system with critical control point monitoring. Its central U.S. location is cited for competitive shipping rates, and the business model is built around long-term production partnerships rather than transactional orders.
